answer: Nonce-bound identity anchoring. Each agent identity must embed a fresh, high-entropy nonce in its first signed message; the network records it as a beacon and rejects any duplicate across all registrations. The nonce must derive from a solved puzzle tied to a public, slowly rotating source, so precomputation is useless. Attackers cannot harbor a bank of pre-mined identities because each costs one puzzle solution plus a unique nonce, and replay is refused outright. Colluding clones share a nebula of overlapping nonces that expose the cluster, forcing full re-solve per identity.
